data.why: 1YJP.pdb already ships in the repo's data/ folder; 1yjp_outlier.pdb is a hand-edited copy (ASN 2 OD1 displaced with B=95, GLN 5 NE2 deleted) for the outlier-screening goal, rlp.csv is a synthetic two-lattice reciprocal-space point set for the split-lattice goal, and agent.html is rewritten so every load path works through URL fetches and <input type=file> uploads instead of drag-and-drop, which the browser agent cannot perform.

goals: Load a crystal structure model (1YJP, the GNNQQNY amyloid peptide) and navigate it in 3D the way a crystallographer inspects a refined structure.
Spot a side chain pushed off its expected position with an unusually high B-factor (ASN 2 OD1, B=95) in the outlier test model.
Notice a missing side-chain atom (GLN 5 NE2) that was deleted from the outlier test model, as would appear when density is too weak to build it.
Load a real electron-density map (2mFo-DFc and mFo-DFc) alongside a model and adjust the sigma (contour) level to judge how well the model fits the density.
Screen a reciprocal-space spot list (rlp.csv) for signs of a split or twinned lattice by distinguishing the two overlapping point sets.
Use the viewer's keyboard/mouse controls (rotate, zoom, clip, label, spin) the way one would in a quick inspection session, similar to using Coot but lighter-weight.

review.summary: The tree is a careful, well-cited record of the model-inspection and lattice-screening work, and most sampled screens show what their nodes claim. But it leaves out electron density, which the paper names as UglyMol's whole point, and the reciprocal-space phase was never reproduced, so it needs a density phase (marked unreached), a few evidence fixes, and confirmed reciprocal replays before filing.
